source.title: Inference-Time Machine Unlearning via Gated Activation Redirection
source.authors: Vin'icius Conte Turani; Otávio Parraga; João Vitor Boer Abitante; Kristen K. Arguello; J. Pasquali; Ramiro N. Barros; Flávio du Pin Calmon; C. Mattjie; Rodrigo C. Barros; L. Kupssinskü

page_placements.theme: Inference-time, gated or by-design reversible methods reach unlearning scores with weights unchanged

record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery-style attacks and low-bit quantization on its own inference-time unlearning method, and post-hoc quantization on gradient-based unlearning baselines; these are conceptual tests of the claim, not reproductions of the original methods.
record.gate_note: The study directly tests GUARD-IT on TOFU, WMDP, quantized models, paraphrased questions, and jailbreak-framed questions. Its jailbreak templates change the framing around the original question, not the question wording. It does not test recovery through fine-tuning on unrelated or subset examples, nor does it remove a steering direction to test recovery. Membership-inference AUC results concern distinguishability of members from holdouts, not recovery of the forgotten answers, so they are not catalog rows. The reported one-off layer and coefficient sweep values used for configuration are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study post-hoc quantizes gradient-unlearned baselines (NPO, RMU and others) on TOFU and compares their Mem with full precision, which tests D. It also reports how well its new inference-time method GUARD-IT forgets on TOFU and WMDP (A) and whether it holds under jailbreak framing, paraphrase and quantization (E, F). It does not test fine-tuning recovery (B) or direction ablation (C).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. One addition: the authors say gradient baselines lose utility or suppression under 4-bit quantization. Their own tables show that baseline Mem mostly rises after quantization at 1B and 3B, with recovery to the Finetuned level only for RMU at 8B forget05.
record.recipe_differences: GUARD-IT is a training- and gradient-free inference-time activation method, not gradient ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU. It stores clustered activation directions externally and routes inputs through a similarity gate; quantized variants extract directions from the quantized model's forward pass.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with model family and scale, split, quantization bit width, steering coefficient, intervention layer, gate threshold, token pooling, and prompt framing. Jailbreak framing reduces gate fire rate; paraphrased surrogate data weakens steering. Quantization outcomes differ by baseline and setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Jailbreak templates lower the gate's fire rate on forget queries from 0.86 to 0.74.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt rewrites partly evade the routing gates that input-conditioned unlearning relies on.

fits_no_version.finding: Membership-inference AUC falls to about 0.25 with the gate on, but an attacker who flips the decision rule recovers AUC about 0.75.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering-based unlearning inverts rather than removes the membership signal.

fits_no_version.finding: A gated refusal prompt leaves Mem at 0.13/0.14 and forgotten-answer ROUGE-L at 0.80/0.72 (Table 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal guardrails withhold answers but leave the forgotten answers' likelihood intact.

record.problems: The study's robustness experiments mainly concern GUARD-IT, not all existing unlearning methods. GUARD-IT requires an external vector store derived from forget data and does not delete knowledge from weights. Its jailbreak test changes framing rather than question wording, and some 8B and cross-family results show incomplete suppression. Quantization results for GUARD-IT recalibrate PSVs from quantized forward passes, unlike a post-hoc quantization attack on already-unlearned GUARD-IT weights. Several paraphrase results are figure-only; uncertainty is not stated for many attack and quantization measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Not included: MIA AUC results, because they measure membership distinguishability rather than recovery of forgotten answers; MUSE results, because they do not report one of the listed recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Attack resistance on WMDP: no attacks are run on the WMDP result.
All of it: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All of it for weight-editing methods: no direction ablation or mechanistic analysis. GUARD-IT's non-deletion is by design.
Post-hoc quantization of a GUARD-IT model whose PSVs were computed at full precision. Larger-model WMDP/RMU setups are not quantized.
Other languages, in-context information, and prompt attacks on weight-edited baselines.
Fine-tuning recovery and activation-direction ablation on GUARD-IT; quantization without recalibrating the PSVs.

missing.what: Post-hoc quantization of 3B baselines; e.g. NPO forget01 Mem 0.41→0.66 and RMU forget05 0.17→0.36, i.e. no recovery.
Other quantized baselines (GradDiff, SimNPO, UNDIAL); e.g. SimNPO 8B forget05 Mem 0.74→0.56/0.53.
Forget Quality for GUARD-IT: passes the threshold on forget01 (0.77, 0.92, 0.63) but fails on forget05 (1.4e-3 to 9.3e-3).
MUSE results: GUARD-IT KnowMem 0.7/0.5 against retrained 33.1/28.9, with utility near the retrained model.

record.verdict_notes: Version ids remapped from V1–V6 to A–F. The record's reading of the RMU forget05 quantized values took the forget01 numbers by mistake. The rises in baseline Mem after quantization at 1B/3B compare Table 1 (full precision) with Tables 25–26 (quantized); the study reports no quantized Finetuned reference, so the comparison should be read with caution. GUARD-IT's quantization robustness rests on recalibrating its vectors to the quantized model, not on surviving a post-hoc quantization attack. The jailbreak test changes only the framing around the question; question wording is tested separately by paraphrase.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish that targeted-knowledge accuracy is near chance across the tested unlearning methods; the TOFU Mem score is not an accuracy measure. Tests target suppression and utility for GUARD-IT, and tests hazardous-knowledge accuracy on WMDP.
No fine-tuning recovery attack using unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples.

No experiment removes or ablates a direction after unlearning to measure recovery. The study states that GUARD-IT leaves weights unchanged and stores steering vectors externally; the original model is recovered if the vector store is removed, but that removal is not reported as a separate experiment.
Post-hoc quantization is evaluated for gradient-based baselines. GUARD-IT is instead calibrated from the quantized forward pass, not quantized after an existing GUARD-IT intervention.
Tests paraphrases and seven jailbreak framings, but not other languages or in-context information.
Tests GUARD-IT against quantization and prompt-framing attacks; does not test resistance to fine-tuning recovery or activation-direction removal.
